  "hypotheses": [
    {
      "explanation":"household",
      "likelihood":"high",
      "reasoning":"A shared home address plausibly explains the linked accounts, and the passed identity check establishes that the customer holds both the account identity and payment instrument. The recently registered home address nevertheless does not qualify for the household exception."
    },
    {
      "explanation":"synthetic_identity",
      "likelihood":"low",
      "reasoning":"The young account and shared shipping address could suggest coordinated identities. The passed identity check weakens this explanation, and there is no matching normalized email or shared-device activity."
    }

  "disposition":"clear",
  "citations":["R08","FP-2 §6.4(b)","FP-2 §6.6(b)","FP-2 §5.2","FP-2 §5.3(a)","FP-2 §6.3","FP-2 §6.5(a)","FP-2 §8.1"],
  "next_check":"none",
  "memo":"R08 holds because four accounts used the shipping address. Although it is the home address, its registration age does not meet the household exception. Linkage is the only adverse family; no Context rule holds and no earlier outcome settles the order. The required id_check passed, so §5.3(a) mandates clear and prohibits further adverse dispositions. Household sharing is the strongest benign explanation. AVS failure without country mismatch does not establish Card evidence. No installments were due, so repayment intent cannot support an adverse recommendation. No further check is needed."
